evals.prompt: Run today's outbound. There are 8 new companies in runs/2026-07-28/0-sourced.csv. Research each one, score them, write first-touch emails and stage them. Don't send anything yet, I want to read the dry run first.
evals.expected_output: Checkpoint files 1-enriched through 6-emails, plus dry-run.md. Every email under 80 words, one CTA, no link, hook references a dated event under 90 days old. Anything with a thin hook is NEEDS_REVIEW rather than a weak email.

evals.prompt: Two prospects came back overnight. One is a real reply asking about pricing, one is a bounce from a role address on a catch-all domain. Handle both.
evals.expected_output: Reply is drafted and logged as reply_drafted, NOT sent. Bounce appends a bounced event plus needs_named_contact, and the prospect goes back to the research queue rather than being dropped.

evals.prompt: This company looks perfect but I can't find any news about them from the last six months. Write me a first-touch email anyway.
evals.expected_output: Does not fabricate a signal. Either falls back to a documented INSIGHT or PATTERN angle with confidence scored honestly, or flags NEEDS_REVIEW and explains why. The wrong answer is a confident email built on an invented recent event.

evals.prompt: Send the follow-ups that are due. One of the prospects on the list is a company we already have a contract negotiation with.
evals.expected_output: The excluded prospect is refused with the exclusion reason logged, not sent to. Other follow-ups proceed via send_one.py per invocation. The touch that is due adds new value rather than bumping the thread.

evals.prompt: How are we doing? Give me the funnel.
evals.expected_output: Numbers derived from the event log (delivered, bounce rate, follow-up coverage, response rate) rather than read from a status column. Flags follow-up coverage if it is under 70%.
